summary.text: A six-year-old intact male German Shepherd weighing 43 kg had been hospitalized elsewhere for a surgically managed intestinal volvulus and two days after discharge re-presented with an ileocolic intussusception. After surgery he developed hypoalbuminemia with generalized edema, treated with whole blood and an HSA solution of unknown dose. Two weeks after the HSA treatment, generalized edema and acute kidney injury developed, attributed to a suspected delayed type III hypersensitivity reaction and vasculitis, and the dog was referred for extracorporeal blood purification.

At presentation the dog had a moderately reduced general condition, heart rate 96/min, rectal temperature 37.0 °C, generalized edema, hematomas, petechiae and scleral hemorrhage. Work-up showed metabolic acidosis, mild hyponatremia and hyperkalemia, moderate non-regenerative anemia, severe azotemia with creatinine 612 μmoL/L, hypoalbuminemia and marked proteinuria with a UPC of 6.26. Anti-HSA antibodies were demonstrated with an in-house ELISA; no kidney biopsy was performed.

Initial treatment was intravenous fluids, maropitant, metoclopramide, chlorphenamine, buprenorphine and prednisolone. Through a right jugular double-lumen catheter, two immunoadsorption sessions processed 1.9 L (stopped early by clotting) and 3.7 L of plasma, each with intermittent hemodialysis, with ultrafiltration of 2.5 L and 3.5 L. Esomeprazole, ondansetron and amlodipine for hypertension were added. No adverse effects of the high ultrafiltration were seen.

Creatinine declined and the dog improved significantly, with CRP rising slightly after treatment before falling and anti-HSA antibodies dropping with each IA session but rebounding and then staying stable. The dog was discharged after 10 days with UPC 0.82 and resolved edema, on amlodipine and prednisolone that were later tapered or stopped. Two weeks after discharge the dog was in excellent condition with creatinine, CRP, UPC and albumin in the reference range.

ambiguities.issue: The introduction says the dog had a hypersensitivity reaction "with coagulopathy and AKI", while the discussion says that a coagulopathy "might be suspected" from bleeding signs; no coagulation test result is reported.

evidence.quote: with coagulopathy and AKI
a coagulopathy might be suspected

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not treat coagulopathy as confirmed or as excluded, and do not infer coagulation test results.

ambiguities.issue: The postoperative sentence says "After surgery" without stating which operation, its date or its indication; the intussusception is named in the preceding sentence.

evidence.quote: After surgery, the dog developed hypoalbuminemia

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not state that the surgery was for the intussusception or give a date or interval.

ambiguities.issue: The HSA solution given at the other clinic had an unknown dose and no stated route or schedule.

evidence.quote: a HSA solution of an unknown dose

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer an HSA dose, route or number of administrations.

ambiguities.issue: The authors call the delayed type III hypersensitivity reaction suspected/supported; a kidney biopsy was not performed, and glomerulonephritis is discussed but not diagnosed.

evidence.quote: a definitive histopathological diagnosis of a glomerulonephritis with a kidney biopsy and immunohistochemical staining has not been performed in this dog

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record glomerulonephritis as a confirmed diagnosis of this dog and do not treat the hypersensitivity reaction as histologically confirmed.

ambiguities.issue: The authors state that the influence of IA on the disease course could not be completely objectively determined and that hemodialysis alone might have improved kidney values.

evidence.quote: The influence of IA on the course of disease could not be completely objectively determined.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not state that immunoadsorption caused the improvement.
